records.distractors: 4N assumes μ=1 or uses normal as friction;1/2 alone is a coefficient without force units. A signed component must be distinguished from the positive modulus.
records.manualArithmetic: In maintained sliding contact Coulomb gives modulus F=μdN=(1/2)4=2 N. On a right-positive axis with rightward relative slip, Fx=−2 N.

Positive coefficient μd is constant within a given trial; no universal bound μd≤1. F=μdN is the positive friction modulus; its vector opposes relative slip and is not necessarily the resultant. Normal load is supplied independently and is not replaced by mg.
